title: Vote share cutoff and policy adoption

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD) with vote share as the running variable and 50% as the cutoff. The key assumption is that ballot initiatives just above and below 50% vote share are comparable in all characteristics except treatment status (policy adoption). This assumes no manipulation of vote shares around the cutoff and that all relevant factors vary smoothly through the threshold.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(rdrobust)

# Read the data
data <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s25_data.csv")

# Center the running variable around the cutoff
data$running_var_centered <- data$running_var - 0.5

# Main RDD analysis using rdrobust
rdd_result <- rdrobust(y = data$y, x = data$running_var, c = 0.5)
print("=== Main RDD Results ===")
print(summary(rdd_result))

# Extract and print the key coefficient
treatment_effect <- rdd_result$coef[1]
se <- rdd_result$se[1]
pvalue <- rdd_result$pval[1]

cat("\n=== Key Results ===\n")
cat("Treatment Effect (Log Spending Change):", round(treatment_effect, 4), "\n")
cat("Standard Error:", round(se, 4), "\n")
cat("P-value:", round(pvalue, 4), "\n")
cat("95% CI: [", round(treatment_effect - 1.96*se, 4), ",", 
    round(treatment_effect + 1.96*se, 4), "]\n")

# Robustness checks
cat("\n=== Robustness Checks ===\n")

# 1. Different bandwidths
bw_half <- rdrobust(y = data$y, x = data$running_var, c = 0.5, h = rdd_result$bws[1]/2)
bw_double <- rdrobust(y = data$y, x = data$running_var, c = 0.5, h = rdd_result$bws[1]*2)

cat("Half bandwidth effect:", round(bw_half$coef[1], 4), 
    "(SE:", round(bw_half$se[1], 4), ")\n")
cat("Double bandwidth effect:", round(bw_double$coef[1], 4), 
    "(SE:", round(bw_double$se[1], 4), ")\n")

# 2. Different polynomial orders
linear <- rdrobust(y = data$y, x = data$running_var, c = 0.5, p = 1)
quadratic <- rdrobust(y = data$y, x = data$running_var, c = 0.5, p = 2)

cat("Linear specification:", round(linear$coef[1], 4), 
    "(SE:", round(linear$se[1], 4), ")\n")
cat("Quadratic specification:", round(quadratic$coef[1], 4), 
    "(SE:", round(quadratic$se[1], 4), ")\n")

# 3. Manual verification with subset near cutoff
near_data <- subset(data, near_cutoff == 1)
manual_model <- lm(y ~ treated + running_var_centered, data = near_data)
cat("Manual OLS on near cutoff:", round(coef(manual_model)["treated"], 4), 
    "(SE:", round(summary(manual_model)$coefficients["treated", "Std. Error"], 4), ")\n")

# Visualization
ggplot(data, aes(x = running_var, y = y)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, aes(color = as.factor(treated))) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  geom_smooth(data = subset(data, running_var < 0.5), method = "loess", se = TRUE, color = "blue") +
  geom_smooth(data = subset(data, running_var >= 0.5), method = "loess", se = TRUE, color = "red") +
  labs(x = "Vote Share", y = "Log Municipal Spending Change", 
       title = "RDD: Policy Adoption and Municipal Spending",
       color = "Policy Adopted") +
  theme_minimal()

# Test for manipulation (McCrary test approximation)
hist_data <- hist(data$running_var, breaks = 50, plot = FALSE)
cat("\n=== Manipulation Check ===\n")
cat("Observations just below cutoff:", sum(data$running_var >= 0.45 & data$running_var < 0.5), "\n")
cat("Observations just above cutoff:", sum(data$running_var >= 0.5 & data$running_var <= 0.55), "\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a positive and significant treatment effect of approximately 0.2-0.4 in log spending change, representing a 20-50% increase in municipal spending on the targeted policy. This is because ballot initiatives that pass (≥50% vote share) should lead to increased government spending on the specific policy area, while those that fail should not trigger such spending increases. The magnitude reflects typical policy implementation costs and the responsiveness of municipal budgets to voter mandates.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Sharp RDD — cutoff = 50% vote share; local linear regression with optimal bandwidth
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Passing the initiative causes a discrete jump in targeted spending
